QF.id: SIA Social Stock Exchange Introduction and Instruments_8

question.text: Hariyali Foundation, an environmental NPO, is designing a 5-year mangrove restoration project and wants to fund it entirely through a ZCZP issuance on NSE-SSE. What should the ZCZP tenure be, per the ICDR framework described in Chapter 2?

answer.text: 3 years (the minimum tenure applicable to all ZCZPs), with renewal thereafter.
7 years, to allow a 2-year monitoring tail after project completion.
Equal to the duration of the project being funded, i.e., 5 years.
10 years, the maximum listing period for any SSE instrument.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per Section 2.3.1.3, ZCZPs 'shall be listed on the SSE and shall carry a tenure equal to the duration of the project that is being funded'. For a 5-year mangrove restoration project, the ZCZP tenure is 5 years. The fund-raising document must specify this duration, within which the stated project/activity must be completed. At maturity, the instrument is written off the NPO's books. The Trap: Option A invents a universal '3-year minimum' — there is no such minimum in the ICDR text for ZCZP; tenure is project-linked. Option B adds a fictional monitoring tail. Option D invents a '10-year cap'. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A/B/C/D/E (AIF) uses a fixed scheme tenure which might mislead here. III-A/III-C (Compliance) distinguishes listing period vs project period. Assessor's Pro-Tip: When certifying year-end impact, cross-tie the ZCZP fund-raising document's stated project duration against the SE's actual project plan — if the NPO plans to continue activities beyond the ZCZP tenure, the post-maturity activities fall outside your assurance scope and need a fresh engagement.
